{{small|(30 June 2012)}} | attendance = 3,129,700 | average attendance = 10,228 | prevseason = [[2010–11 Indonesia Super League|2010–11]] | nextseason = [[2013 Indonesia Super League|2013]] }} The '''2011–12 Indonesia Super League''' was the 4th season of the [[Indonesia Super League]] (ISL), a fully professional football competition as the top tier of the [[Association football|football]] league pyramid in [[Indonesia]]. The season began on 1 December 2011. [[Persipura Jayapura|Persipura]] were the defending champions, having won their 3rd [[List of Indonesian football champions|league title]] the [[2010–11 Indonesia Super League|previous season]]. This season was also the first season of ISL organized without authorization from [[Football Association of Indonesia|PSSI]] due to internal conflict. PSSI under chairman Johar Arifin officially decided to replace ISL as a top level with the [[Indonesian Premier League]]. It was then recognized by other faction of PSSI under chairman [[La Nyalla Matalatti]]. After the signing of the [[Memorandum of understanding|MoU]] between [[Djohar Arifin Husein]] (PSSI) and La Nyalla Matalitti (KPSI-PSSI) that was initiated by [[FIFA]] and the [[Asian Football Confederation|AFC]] through the AFC force task, Indonesia Super League was under the control of the joint committee to remain manageable by PT Liga Indonesia until the establishment of a new professional competition by the committee.{{cite web|url=http://bolanews.com/read/sepakbola/indonesia/8968-Dua-PSSI-Sepakat-Perbaiki-Sepak-Bola-Indonesia.html|title=Dua PSSI sepakat perbaiki sepakbola Indonesia|publisher=bolanews.com|access-date=7 June 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222223149/http://bolanews.com/read/sepakbola/indonesia/8968-Dua-PSSI-Sepakat-Perbaiki-Sepak-Bola-Indonesia.html|archive-date=22 February 2014|url-status=usurped}} ==Teams== [[Persibo Bojonegoro|Persibo]], [[Persema Malang|Persema]], [[Bontang F.C.|Bontang]] and [[PSM Makassar|PSM]] were joined to [[2011–12 Indonesian Premier League]]. They were replaced by the best three teams from the [[2010–11 Liga Indonesia Premier Division]], [[Persiba Bantul]], [[Mitra Kukar]] and [[Persiraja Banda Aceh|Persiraja]]. Fourth-placed Premier Division sides [[Persidafon Dafonsoro|Persidafon]] were promoted to [[Indonesia Super League]] after winning the relegation/promotion play-off against 15th placed [[2010–11 Indonesia Super League]] sides [[Bontang F.C.|Bontang]] by score 3–2. [[2010–11 Liga Indonesia Premier Division]] best-eight teams sides [[PSAP Sigli]], [[Persiram Raja Ampat|Persiram]], [[Gresik United]] and [[PSMS Medan|PSMS]] replaced [[Persijap Jepara|Persijap]],
